exercise1.prompt: A Dog class with __init__(name, breed), then a Buddy the Golden Retriever

cases.name: the dog keeps the name it was given
prints the name and the breed

hiddenCases.name: Dog is a class with an __init__
hiddenCases.describe: a Dog class whose __init__ sets up each new dog

hiddenCases.name: a different dog gets its own breed
prints the breed too
hiddenCases.describe: the breed printed alongside the name

exercise1.hint: __init__ receives the values as parameters, so the attributes have to be built from those parameters rather than written into the class. A second dog with different details is the test of that.

exercise2.prompt: A Circle class taking radius, with color defaulting to Red

cases.name: the circle keeps the radius it was given
prints the radius and the colour

hiddenCases.name: Circle is a class with an __init__
hiddenCases.describe: a Circle class whose __init__ takes the radius

hiddenCases.name: every circle starts out red without being told to
a different radius is kept as given

exercise2.hint: The first parameter of every method is self, even when the method takes other things as well. Without it Python has no way to say which circle the radius belongs to.

choices: When the class statement is read
Every time an object is created from the class
Only when you call it by name
questions.explain: Creating an object is what calls __init__, which is why it is the place to set up that object's own data.

choices: The particular object the method was called on
A keyword Python requires by that exact spelling
questions.explain: self is the object in front of the dot. It is an ordinary parameter name by convention, not a keyword, but everyone spells it self.

questions.prompt: Put these lines in order so a Dog class is defined and one dog is made.
questions.explain: The class has to exist before it can be called, and the assignment to self.name sits inside __init__, indented one level further.

questions.prompt: Inside __init__, the line that stores the name on this particular dog is ___ = name.
questions.explain: Without the self. prefix you have created a local variable that disappears the moment __init__ returns.
